newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese troops in HK hold open days for public.
newsitem.headline: Chinese troops in HK hold open days for public.

text.p: China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) garrison in Hong Kong said on Thursday it had launched a campaign to forge ties with the territory's people.

The 4,700-strong Chinese garrison said in a statement issued through Hong Gong's government information agency that it had opened its bases to hundreds of local visitors in the past week to mark the PLA's 70th anniversary, which falls on Friday.
On Thursday 130 trade unionists visited the naval base on Stonecutters' Island, in the centre of the world's busiest harbour.
The statement said the visitors, from a pro-China trade union, praised the PLA soldiers for their good discipline.
The garrison's air base at Sek Kong also hosted a forum with 60 representatives from the rural New Territories, enabling locals to glimpse the soldiers' life inside the camp, it said.
Representatives from southern Hong Kong Island and a China-funded company held a friendly soccer match and ping-pong game with the PLA troops during their visit.
The PLA's political commissar Major-General Xiong Ziren said the PLA would unite with the territory's 6.4 million people to build a better Hong Kong, now a Special Administrative Region of China.

The statement said the troops had not broken any laws since they took up defence duties in Hong Kong on July 1, when they replaced the British garrison after London handed Hong Kong back to China, ending 156 years of colonial rule.
However, the garrision has been criticised by local media for giving Chineses state media privileged access.
Many in Hong Kong view the PLA's presence with some alarm due to its role in the bloody 1989 crackdown of a student-led democracy protest in Beijing's Tiananmen Square.
Hundreds, possibly thousands, were killed when the PLA opened fire on unarmed civilians.
